metadata.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models

problem.value: Mathematical reasoning presents a major challenge for language models due to its structured and complex nature.

evidence.quote: Mathematical reasoning poses a significant challenge for language models due to its complex and structured nature.

problem.value: Top models like GPT-4 and Gemini-Ultra are closed-source, while accessible open-source models trail significantly in performance.

evidence.quote: However, cutting-edge models such as GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) and Gemini-Ultra (Anil et al., 2023) are not publicly available, and the currently accessible open-source models considerably trail behind in performance.

contributions.value: The authors introduce DeepSeekMath 7B, trained on a large math-related corpus using code pretraining and a data selection pipeline.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we introduce DeepSeekMath 7B, which continues pretraining DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B with 120B math-related tokens sourced from Common Crawl, together with natural language and code data.

contributions.value: The authors propose Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a memory-efficient variant of PPO for reinforcement learning.

evidence.quote: Second, we introduce Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a variant of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), that enhances mathematical reasoning abilities while concurrently optimizing the memory usage of PPO.

contributions.value: The research contribution includes scalable math pre-training and the exploration and analysis of reinforcement learning.

evidence.quote: Our contribution includes scalable math pre-training, along with the exploration and analysis of reinforcement learning.
Mathematical reasoning poses a significant challenge for language models due to its complex and structured nature.

method_summary.value: An iterative pipeline is used to build the DeepSeekMath Corpus from Common Crawl, starting with a seed corpus and training a fastText model to gather math web pages over four iterations.

evidence.quote: As depicted in Figure 2, we present an iterative pipeline that demonstrates how to systematically gather a large-scale mathematical corpus from Common Crawl, starting with a seed corpus (e.g., a small but high-quality collection of math-related dataset).

method_summary.value: To prevent benchmark contamination, web pages containing 10-gram strings (or 3-to-9-gram exact matches) matching evaluation benchmarks are filtered out from the math training corpus.

evidence.quote: The filtering criteria are as follows: any text segment containing a 10-gram string that matches exactly with any sub-string from the evaluation benchmarks is removed from our math training corpus.

method_summary.value: DeepSeekMath-Base 7B is initialized with DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B and trained for 500B tokens on a mix of DeepSeekMath Corpus, AlgebraicStack, arXiv, GitHub code, and natural language data.

evidence.quote: Our model is initialized with DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B (Guo et al., 2024) and trained for 500B tokens.

method_summary.value: Mathematical instruction-tuning is performed on DeepSeekMath-Base using a dataset of 776K examples covering chain-of-thought, program-of-thought, and tool-integrated reasoning formats.

evidence.quote: In this section, we introduce DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B which undergoes mathematical instruction tuning based on DeepSeekMath-Base.

method_summary.value: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is proposed as a reinforcement learning algorithm that eliminates the need for a separate value function by using the average reward of multiple sampled outputs as the baseline.

evidence.quote: To address this, as shown in Figure 4, we propose Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which obviates the need for additional value function approximation as in PPO, and instead uses the average reward of multiple sampled outputs, produced in response to the same question, as the baseline.

novelty.value: GRPO avoids the memory and computational burden of approximating a separate value function in PPO by using the average reward of multiple sampled outputs for the same question as the baseline.

First, we choose OpenWebMath (Paster et al., 2023), a collection of high-quality mathematical web texts, as our initial seed corpus.
Specifically, we randomly select 500,000 data points from the seed corpus as positive training examples and another 500,000 web pages from Common Crawl as negative ones.
After four iterations of data collection, we end up with 35.5M mathematical web pages, totaling 120B tokens.

limitations.value: The conclusion regarding arXiv papers being ineffective has certain limitations and unstudied aspects.

evidence.quote: However, this conclusion has its limitations and should be taken with a grain of salt.

limitations.value: The model has weaker performance on geometry and theorem-proof compared to closed-source models.

evidence.quote: Although DeepSeekMath achieves impressive scores on quantitative reasoning benchmarks, its capability on geometry and theorem-proof are relatively weaker than closed models.

limitations.value: DeepSeekMath shows similar performance in zero-shot and few-shot evaluation due to model scale limitations.

evidence.quote: In addition, restricted by the model scale, DeepSeekMath is worse than GPT-4 on few-shot capability.

claims.value: DeepSeekMath 7B scores 51.7% on the competition-level MATH benchmark without external toolkits.

evidence.quote: DeepSeekMath 7B has achieved an impressive score of 51.7% on the competition-level MATH benchmark without relying on external toolkits and voting techniques, approaching the performance level of Gemini-Ultra and GPT-4.

claims.value: Self-consistency over 64 samples achieves 60.9% on the MATH benchmark.

evidence.quote: Self-consistency over 64 samples from DeepSeekMath 7B achieves 60.9% on MATH.

claims.value: DeepSeekMath-Base 7B achieves 64.2% on GSM8K and 36.2% on the MATH dataset, outperforming Minerva 540B.

evidence.quote: The evaluation results indicate that the large-scale corpus is of high quality, as our base model DeepSeekMath-Base 7B achieves 64.2% on GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) and 36.2% on the competition-level MATH dataset (Hendrycks et al., 2021), outperforming Minerva 540B (Lewkowycz et al., 2022a).

claims.value: GRPO provides improvements on in-domain and out-of-domain mathematical tasks.

evidence.quote: By solely using a subset of English instruction tuning data, GRPO obtains a substantial improvement over the strong DeepSeekMath-Instruct, including both in-domain (GSM8K: 82.9% → 88.2%, MATH: 46.8% → 51.7%) and out-of-domain mathematical tasks (e.g., CMATH: 84.6% → 88.8%) during the reinforcement learning phase.
